text:
ashwin: kicking off a synthetic burst window test now against eu-west-1 pool to validate admission and queueing behavior

infra-bot: loadgen scheduled by ashwin at 2026-11-05T09:00:10Z — test id: lg-20261105-09-eu 

marta: copy — what profile are you using? short-chat vs long-stream?

ashwin: short-chat profile, mean tokens 64, p95 latency target 120ms, burst window 30s, sustained for 5m after ramp

kevin: reminder: eu-west-1 currently has 80% GPU sat for rt-variants; admission thresholds set to 75% active_by_slot, so we should hit backpressure quickly

olivia: can you paste the admission config? want to check rate-limit vs queue-size fallback

ashwin: sure — config snippet: ```
admission_policy:
  max_inflight_per_gpu: 48
  queue_size_limit: 1024
  burst_window_seconds: 30
  admission_cpu_pct_threshold: 0.85
  admission_gpu_util_threshold: 0.75
  overflow_fallback: route:dedicated_low_priority
```

marta: thanks. two quick asks: 1) include a run with artificial network jitter to see if queueing amplifies, 2) annotate when model-fallback triggers

ashwin: will add jitter + a second run with fallback disabled. starting run #1 now (no jitter)

infra-bot: run lg-20261105-09-eu started, workers=120, target_qps=2000, ramp=20s, sustain=5m

kevin: early telemetry: queue_depth spiked to 900 within 18s, median latency stayed ~110ms but p99 jumped to 540ms

olivia: that p99 is concerning — did admission drop incoming QPS or did it just back up?

ashwin: admission controller started returning 429s at ~22s, logs show ``admit=false reason=capacity`` then we saw queue drain slowly, fallback routing didn't trigger since dedicated_low_priority pool was flagged draining

marta: can you paste the admission log line?

ashwin: ``2026-11-05T09:00:32Z admit_controller.go:214 admit=false pool=eu-west-1-rt gpu_util=0.78 inflight=51 queue=912 threshold=0.75``

kevin: interesting — gpu_util under threshold but inflight > max_inflight_per_gpu, so admission checks both. maybe we need to surface combined signals in the console (gpu_util vs inflight)

olivia: cost note — with this burst profile we consumed ~3.6k GPU-minutes in 5m, estimate ~ $540 for the run if using on-demand pricing. add to cost tracker? :money_with_wings:

ashwin: logged cost in the spreadsheet. running jittered run now (run #2) with 20-50ms added latency to host networking

infra-bot: run lg-20261105-09-eu-2 started, jitter=20-50ms, workers=120, qps=2000

kevin: telemetry #2: queue_depth faster growth, p95 200ms, p99 980ms, admission started earlier at ~14s

marta: does the admission controller handle jitter differently? looks like inflight spikes due to slower response times, so thresholding on gpu_util alone is insufficient

ashwin: agree. proposal: modify admission check to prioritize estimated effective_slots = inflight * (observed_latency / target_latency). if effective_slots > max_inflight_per_gpu then admit=false

olivia: +1 for effective_slots heuristic. also suggest limiting client retry TTL to avoid thundering retries when 429s happen (exponential backoff with jitter)

kevin: can we simulate client retries in next run to validate? I suspect retries will saturate dedicated_low_priority when fallback is enabled

ashwin: will schedule run #3 with retries enabled (clients retry up to 3 times with base=200ms) and fallback route available

infra-bot: run lg-20261105-09-eu-3 started, retries=3, fallback=enabled

marta: live note — fallback pool accepted ~35% of overflow but its GPU nodes were preemptible and had 2x latency, increased end-to-end errors from 0.2% -> 1.8%

kevin: that's a tolerability tradeoff we need to document. fallback keeps service alive but raises error budget and tail latency for some customers

olivia: next steps from test: 1) implement effective_slots heuristic in admission controller, 2) add retry guidance to docs + client SDK with adaptive backoff, 3) add console panel for inflight vs gpu_util overlay, 4) create cost estimate for burst windows and add guardrail on scheduled tests to warn about >$100 cost

ashwin: filing follow-ups: ENG-RUNTIME-PT1 (admission heuristic), ENG-DEVEX-PT2 (retry guidance), MON-PT3 (console panel), FIN-PT4 (test cost warning). I'll post PR links in this thread when ready

sre-oncall: heads-up — please avoid scheduling heavy burst tests during peak biz hours in us-east-1 next week; we had an incident last month when scheduled jobs overlapped with a customer migration

ashwin: noted, will coordinate change window with you. thanks everyone for quick feedback :thumbsup:
